segments.expected: "The Board doesn't say he was wrong," she said. "The Board says it doesn't know, and that a country that doesn't know shouldn't be one engine while it finds out. That's the Works' reading. It's the only one in this hall that isn't a reading of what's coming. It's a reading of what to do in the meantime." She folded her hands. "Write that the Board heard Mr. Halden, and that it doesn't say he was wrong, and that it doesn't say he was right, and that it orders the banks on their own counts anyway, because a fitter's rule is all it's got."

segments.expected: They went down the trap into the cellar one at a time by the ladder, the ward line first, then Nairn with his blade, then Pike, then Kiva, one-handed, with Pru below her on the ladder's foot with a hand ready that she did not need. The cellar was low and black and smelled of wet coal and the tannery. Mace's lamp, set on the copper, showed the floor: stone, still dark with Wednesday's water at the low end, and in the corner where it had lain longest, three grey shapes standing on a thread of grey, shoulder to shoulder, very still, like three men waiting for a door to open.
